Some of the dozens of declassified files released by the Pentagon on Friday on unidentified flying objects include plans to build an underground storage facility in Nevada, that would hold “recovered hardware” and “exotic material or tissue.”

The curious details were shared in a 538-page report by the former government contractor Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) in 2009. The company, which shut down in 2020, also documented in the report its efforts to investigate sightings of UFOs — also known as unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) ― and interview and study eyewitnesses.

The underground, camouflaged facility would be built on the company’s property in North Las Vegas. It would feature, according to the cited architectural plans, 3-foot-thick walls and multiple security doors, including a “thick vault steel door,” which would be accessed by a concrete tunnel, according to the document.

Here, workers would be able “to store exotic material or tissue that the organization could obtain,” with 24-hour armed guards patrolling, it said.

CBS News, which first reported on the documents, noted that there’s no public record indicating that the facility was ever built.

Just several months after the report was made, a Defense Intelligence Agency official reportedly said BAASS’s reports had “limited value” and the Pentagon’s study of potential future aerospace threats ended in 2012.

BAASS’s report also includes detailed interviews with UFO experts and various alleged witnesses, some of whom had their fingernails clipped and taken for analysis for potential radiation exposure.

The report also mentions researchers inquiring about an “alien” chip that was purportedly found implanted in a Brazilian military official’s neck and later extracted by doctors in the U.S.

BAASS included a photo of the chip in its report and said it was instructed to “tell no one of its existence.”

Another large section in the report offers summaries of papers that BAASS contracted the research organization EarthTech International to produce. The research topics included “interstellar travel via traversable wormholes,” “theory and experiments of invisibility cloaking” and “warp drive, dark energy, and the manipulation of extra dimensions.” EarthTech International, which is located in Austin, lists information on some of these topics on its website.

Friday’s file release was the eighth since May. The Defense Department said it will release more files on a rolling basis.
